session_note: Arkansas's 95th General Assembly 2026 fiscal session convened 2026-04-08 and adjourned sine die 2026-04-29; as a constitutionally limited even-year fiscal session it is restricted primarily to budget/appropriation matters, so any nonappropriation bill first required a resolution authorizing its introduction, and the King/McNair resolutions on crypto-mining and data centers failed to secure that authorization.

decisions.notes: Directly verified via arkleg.state.ar.us: 3 of 6 Senate resolutions (SR7, SR8, SR12) and 3 of 6 House resolutions (HR1010, HR1011, HR1015); SR9-SR11 and HR1012-HR1014 were not individually pulled but are presumed uniform given the identical filing dates, identical procedural pattern, and identical outcome across every resolution actually checked. All Senate resolutions failed adoption on third reading 2026-04-21 (before formal Sine Die death 2026-04-29); all House resolutions never left the House Rules Committee. One minor variation: HR1015's lead sponsor is listed as Rep. Beaty Jr. rather than Rep. McNair, though this does not affect the disposition. Because none of these authorizing resolutions passed, none of the underlying nonappropriation bills (crypto-mining local control, extraordinary electricity-use fees, foreign hardware/software restrictions, money-transmitter licensing, six-month land-acquisition/construction notice, water-use monitoring) were ever formally introduced as bills in the 2026 fiscal session.
